LESSON: WRITING 3.3.2 WRITING SYLLABLES. (BA - BU, DA-DU)

Grade: SNE  /  hearing-impairment / PP2
Subject: General
Strand: Strand 3
Topic 3.3: Writing 3.3.2 Writing syllables. (ba - bu, da-du)
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Writing 3.3.2 Writing syllables. (ba - bu, da-du), part of Strand 3 in SNE  /  hearing-impairment / PP2 General.

Key inquiry question: Which materials do we use for writing? 2. How do we sit when writing? 3.How do we position a book when writing?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Writing 3.3.2 Writing syllables. (ba - bu, da-du) together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Critical thinking and problem solving: Interpretation and inference skills as learner joins letter sounds to write the syllables

appropriately.

• Learning to learn: Learning independently as learner realizes that syllables other than being written on books can be written in

the air and be modelled.

49

• Creativity and Imagination: originality as learner draws and colors syllables.

Values:
• Respect: Patience as learner works with others in harmony while modelling and coloring syllables.

• Social justice: Cooperation as learners ensure fairness in sharing of the drawing, modelling and coloring items.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
• Personal hygiene awareness as learner washes hands with clean water and soap after coloring and modelling

experiences.

Link to other Activity Areas:

Creative Activities(Art and Craft)as learner engage in colouring and modelling activities in the same way they

model and colour syllables
